rule.title: Focus Trapping and ESC Key Dismissal in Modal Dialogs
rule.statement: Modal dialogs must trap keyboard focus within the dialog container and dismiss immediately upon pressing the Escape key.
rule.rationale: Without focus trapping, keyboard and screen-reader users tab behind the modal into the backdrop, losing their place and rendering the application unusable.
rule.implementation_guidance: Use Radix UI Dialog primitives (shadcn/ui Dialog) which handle focus trapping, ARIA roles, and Escape listener out of the box.

forbidden.example: Building a custom modal with a raw <div> and fixed positioning without focus trapping.

source.evidence_quote: Modal dialogs require user interaction before returning to the parent window. Focus must be trapped inside the dialog, and Escape should provide a clean cancel.

rule.title: Explicit Two-Step Confirmation for Destructive Actions
rule.statement: Destructive operations (e.g. deleting knowledge bases, revoking keys) must require explicit confirmation with the resource name stated, and default focus must NOT rest on the destructive button.
rule.rationale: Accidental clicks or pressing Enter immediately upon dialog open can permanently destroy user data if default focus is on the Delete action.
rule.implementation_guidance: Style the confirm button in Destructive Red. Focus the Cancel button by default. Require typing the resource name for critical bulk deletes.

forbidden.example: Using window.confirm('Are you sure?') or auto-focusing the red Delete button on modal open.

source.evidence_quote: For irreversible or destructive operations, require an explicit confirmation step. Clearly state what will be lost and never make the destructive action the default choice.
